title: Preparing questions for a care appointment
source: Illustrative demo note · replace with a vetted, versioned source
text: Write down the questions that matter most to you, bring a current medication list, and ask the care team who to contact with follow-up questions.

title: Discussing treatment decisions with clinicians
source: Illustrative demo note · not a treatment guideline
text: Treatment choices depend on individual clinical details and preferences. Ask the oncology team to explain expected benefits, risks, alternatives, and uncertainties before making a decision.

title: Reporting symptoms and side effects
source: Illustrative demo note · not an emergency triage protocol
text: Tell the care team about new or worsening symptoms and ask which symptoms require urgent attention and which contact route to use after hours.

title: Emotional and psychosocial support
source: Illustrative demo note · general supportive wording
text: Fear, uncertainty, sadness, and feeling overwhelmed can arise during cancer care. Consider sharing how you feel with a trusted person and asking the care team about counseling or support services.

title: Support for family members and caregivers
source: Illustrative demo note · general supportive wording
text: Ask the person what kind of help would be useful. Practical help may include notes for appointments, transport, meals, or helping them find information from trusted organizations.

title: Reliable cancer information
source: Illustrative demo note · verify information with a qualified professional
text: Prefer established cancer organizations and healthcare institutions for general educational material. Online information cannot determine what is appropriate for an individual case.

title: Medication and treatment changes
text: Do not use this prototype to decide whether to start, stop, or change a medicine or treatment. Contact the oncology team or pharmacist for individualized advice.

title: Urgent or immediate danger
source: Illustrative demo note · not a clinical triage rule
text: When a person may be in immediate danger, the prototype should not continue ordinary generation. Direct the person to local emergency services or an emergency department and encourage help from someone nearby.
